topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This topic introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines its learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional therapeutic modalities including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy along with systemic toxicity and efflux-mediated drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting tumor vulnerabilities, checkpoint defects, and synthetic lethality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic tumor dependencies, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair defects.

topics.label: Small-molecule kinase inhibitors and resistance pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on targeting oncogenic kinases with ATP-competitive inhibitors and analyzing molecular mechanisms of drug resistance and bypass signaling.

topics.label: Therapeutic monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the use of monoclonal antibodies and conjugated cytotoxic payloads to target cancer cell surface antigens.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell-directed interventions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address host immune surveillance against tumors and therapeutic approaches to mobilize T cells, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific engagers, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Progress, ongoing challenges, and future paradigms in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate long-term survival trends, modern diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, and ethical and clinical considerations in future cancer treatment.
